City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 7, 2021
   C. ORDINANCE NO. 677 – CHANGING THE DATE OF THE CITY’S GENERAL
  MUNICIPAL ELECTION TO COMPLY WITH NEW STATE OF CALIFORNIA
  LEGISLATION - ADOPTION

  Adoption of Ordinance No. 677 would change the date of the City’s general
  municipal elections from March of Even-Numbered Years to the Statewide
  General Election cycle beginning in 2022.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council waive reading and adopt Ordinance
  No. 677 entitled, “An Ordinance of the City Council of the City of San Gabriel,
  California, Changing the Date of the City’s General Municipal Elections from
  March of Even-Numbered Year to the Date of the Statewide General Election
  of Each Even-Numbered Year Beginning in 2022, Adjusting Terms of Office
  and Repealing Ordinance No. 640-C.S.”

  D. LEAGUE OF CALIFORNIA CITIES ANNUAL CONFERENCE RESOLUTIONS
  PACKET

  The League of California Cities will consider two resolutions at its annual
  conference on September 22 through 24. The League would like each
  member city to establish a position on the resolutions prior to the annual
  meeting, and provide direction to the voting delegate.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council give direction to the voting delegate
  and alternate to vote in favor of the proposed League of California Cities
  (League) annual resolutions. Alternatively, the City Council may wish to pull
  this item from the Consent Calendar for discussion.

  E. ADOPTION AT SECOND READING OF ORDINANCE NO. 676: ZONE
  CHANGE/SPECIFIC PLAN AMENDMENT TO CHANGE ZONING FROM R-1
  AND MU/T TO CC/T (PLANNING CASE NO. ZC20-001; 150 HOVEY
  AVENUE, 152 HOVEY AVENUE, 1533 MANLEY DRIVE, AND 1535 MANLEY
  DRIVE)

  Adoption of Ordinance No. 676 would change the Zoning of properties at 150
  Hovey Avenue, 152 Hovey Avenue, 1533 Manley Drive, and 1535 Manley Drive
  from R-1 and MU/T to CC/T.

  3
City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 7, 2021
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council waive second reading and adopt
  Ordinance No. 676 entitled, “An Ordinance of the City Council of the City of
  San Gabriel, California, Approving Planning Case No. ZC-20-001, for a Zone
  Change for Properties at 150 Hovey Avenue, 152 Hovey Avenue, 1533 Manley
  Drive, and 1535 Manley Drive.”

  F. COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT WITH LOS ANGELES COUNTY FOR A
  PROJECT TO RESURFACE SEVERAL CITY STREET SEGMENTS ADJACENT
  TO THE COUNTY STREET SEGMENTS AT AN ESTIMATED COST OF
  $597,000

  On behalf of the City of San Gabriel, the Los Angeles County Department of
  Public Works (LACDPW) is to perform pavement preservation work and
  construction or modification of curb ramps for the City street segments, which
  are jurisdictionally shared between the City and the County. Due to the scope
  and cost of the project, County policy requires a Cooperative Agreement to
  be executed to perform pavement preservation improvement for City of San
  Gabriel street segments. The currently estimated City jurisdiction share cost
  of the project is $597,000, which will be credited through Federal Surface
  Transportation Program-Local (STP-L) to the County in lieu of Cash.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the Mayor to execute the
  Cooperative Agreement between the City and Los Angeles County and
  approve the assignment of $597,000 of future available STP-L funds to the
  County in lieu of cash payment.

  G. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 21-43 APPROVING A BUDGET
  AMENDMENT FOR CITYWIDE PAVEMENT MANAGEMENT SYSTEM

  A Pavement Management System is a tool for understanding the condition of
  the street system, analyzing financial needs, and developing cost-effective
  repair strategies. Since 2000, the City has utilized the Pavement Management
  System (PMS) developed by the Metropolitan Transportation Commission
  (MTC). Proposition C (which provides approximately $600,000 annually in
  transportation funding to the City) requires that the City maintain a PMS and
  regularly update it every three years in order to receive funding. The last
  update to the PMS was in 2018. A $41,000 budget amendment appropriating
  Metro - Proposition C funds in the Fiscal Year 2021-22 Budget to update the

  4
City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 7, 2021
   Citywide Pavement Management System conducted by the Los Angeles
  County Public Works Department, includes a 15% contingency.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Adopt Resolution No. 21-43 amending the Fiscal Year 2021-22 budget by
  appropriating Proposition C funds to budget account 181-800-46-22-000
  in the amount of $41,000, which includes a 15% contingency; and
  2. Authorize the City Manager to approve a Purchase Order to the Los
  Angeles County Public Works Department in an amount not to exceed
  $41,000, which includes a 15% contingency.

  H. ADOPTION AT SECOND READING OF ORDINANCE NO. 674 AMENDING
  CHAPTER 92 OF THE SAN GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE TO INCLUDE
  VOLUNTARY CAT LICENSING

  Adoption of Ordinance No. 674 would add voluntary cat licensing to help
  support animal care and control in the community and facilitate reuniting cats
  with their owners.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council waive reading and adopt Ordinance
  No. 674 entitled, “An Ordinance of the City Council of San Gabriel, California,
  Amending Chapter 92 of the San Gabriel Municipal Code Relating to Cat
  Licensing.”

  5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

  6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

  7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. AGENDA TRANSLATION OPTIONS AND RESOLUTION NO. 21-40
  APPROPRIATING FUNDS FOR AGENDA TRANSLATION SERVICES

  At City Manager Lazzaretto’s request, staff researched options for City Council
  and Human Equity, Access and Relations (HEAR) Commission meeting agenda
  translation into Chinese and Spanish in order to expand accessibility to the
  community. Subsequently, the HEAR Commission, in its Annual Workplan
  approved by the City Council on June 15, 2021, recommended translation of
  City Council agendas into Chinese and Spanish by the start of 2022. During

  5
City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 7, 2021
   the same meeting, the City Council expressed interest in adding Vietnamese
  to the languages to be considered for agenda translation. Expanding
  accessibility to the community, particularly for non-English speakers, is
  consistent with California law and the City’s fundamental values of
  transparency and diversity.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council consider one of the following options
  or give other direction:

  1. Proceed with translation of City Council and HEAR Commission agendas
  into Chinese, Spanish, and Vietnamese by ASTA-USA at an approximate
  cost of $40,000 annually; and adopt Resolution No. 21-40 appropriating
  $40,000 for agenda translation service.
  2. Proceed with translation of City Council and HEAR Commission agendas
  by ASTA-USA into Chinese and Spanish only, for now, at an approximate
  cost of $26,000 for agenda translation services.
  3. Proceed with translation of City Council and all City commission agendas
  into Chinese, Spanish, and Vietnamese using ASTA-USA, at a greater cost
  than Option 1. Staff would return with an approximate annual cost for the
  City Council’s authorization.
  4. Add Google Translate to the City’s website agenda section; do not pay for
  translation services.
  5. No change from current practice – agendas in English only.

  B. RESOLUTION NO. 21-37 – AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2021-22
  BUDGET TO ACCEPT DONATIONS FROM KIWANIS CLUB OF SAN
  GABRIEL

  Kiwanis Club of San Gabriel has generously donated funds to support various
  programs and services within the Community Services, Police, and Public
  Works Departments. This donation is to support the following programs and
  services: San Gabriel Police Explorers, Camp SG, swimming lessons, and
  various benches to be placed in the City parks.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council accept a donation of $5,579.52 from
  San Gabriel Kiwanis and adopt Resolution No. 21-37 amending the Fiscal Year
  2021-22 budget to reflect the donations to the City’s account.

  6
City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 7, 2021
   C. AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN ACT FUNDS – PRESENTATION AND
  DISCUSSION

  Signed into law on March 11, 2021, the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA)
  provides $350 billion in Coronavirus Fiscal Recovery Funds to state, local,
  territorial, and Tribal governments to respond to their present needs and
  build the foundation for a strong recovery. The City of San Gabriel was
  allocated $9,544,689 in ARPA funds, which was based on City population. This
  report provides an analysis of ARPA funds including timeline for use,
  reporting, eligible and ineligible uses, and current planned uses.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council discuss, receive and file the report.

  8. PUBLIC COMMENT

  9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

  11. CLOSED SESSION

  12. ADJOURNMENT

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, September 21,

  C. AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN ACT FUNDS- PRESENTATION AND DISCUSSION

  Finance Director Kaholokula made the staff presentation.

  Clarification discussion included that the purpose of this item was brainstorm ing
  and informational regarding use of American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) Funds;
  premium pay as a one-time bonus for eligible staff and associated Public
  Employees Retirement System implications; current fiber-optic project funding and
  details; and using ARPA funds for federal grant match requirements.

I  There was no public comment.

  Discussion included small business grants, loans, and incentives; premium pay for
  staff instrumental in providing COVID-related services; broadband infrastructu re;
  growing revenue reserves; hiring an additional staff person to deal with COVID-19
  recovery and relief, ARPA funds, and grants; partnering with businesses and non-
  profits; use of ARPA funds in other areas would bring the City closer to refinanc ing
  the Public Works loan and afford ing a new police facility; already budgeted ARPA
  funds; rent assistance; and Senate Bill 156 provisions for broadband funding .

I  budget for the HEAR Commission.

  cost for Google Translate; Google Translate set-up and use; one-time translation
  of non-changing portions of the agendas; translation as a tool to increase access
  and engagement; fisca l considerations; comparison of Google Translate and
  professional translation for future decisions on agenda translation methodology;
  and Traditional versus Simpl ified Chinese.

  A motion was made by Vice Mayor Ding, seconded by Council Member Pu, to:

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 4 of 6  September 7, 202 1
   1. Proceed with translation of City Council and HEAR Commission agendas into
  Chinese, Spanish, and Vietnamese by ASTA-USA at an approximate cost of
  $40,000 annually; and adopt Resolution No. 21 -40 appropriating $40,000 for
  agenda translation service.
  2. Add Google Translate to the City's website agenda section.

  the City Council might wish to agendize the matter for a future meeting. There was a

  COG activities regarding homelessness and transportation matters; and stated he will
  bring back information from the upcoming League of California Cities conference.

  Council Member Menchaca reported on the San Gabriel Mission's Fiesta; announced
